title: Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA)

obligations.text: A non-bank entity authorised as AD Category-II that facilitates current account transactions not prohibited under FEMA (other than purchase or sale of goods or service) shall not fall within the purview of PA-CB business.
obligations.applies_to: Non-bank entity authorised as AD Category-II facilitating current account transactions not prohibited under FEMA
obligations.quote: A non-bank entity authorised as AD Category-II, and facilitating current account transactions not prohibited under FEMA (other than purchase or sale of goods or service), shall not fall within the purview of PA – CB business.

obligations.text: A non-bank entity shall seek authorisation for operating as a PA by submitting an application through RBI's online portal.
obligations.quote: A non-bank entity shall seek authorisation for operating as a PA by submitting an application through RBI’s online portal .

obligations.text: An entity regulated by any financial sector regulator shall apply for PA authorisation along with a No Objection Certificate from such regulator(s), within 45 days of obtaining the NOC.
obligations.applies_to: entity regulated by any financial sector regulator
obligations.deadline: within 45 days of obtaining the NOC
obligations.quote: An entity, regulated by any of the financial sector regulator(s), shall apply along with a ‘No Objection Certificate’ (NOC) from such regulator(s), within 45 days of obtaining the NOC.

obligations.text: A non-bank PA shall be a company incorporated in India under the Companies Act, 2013.
obligations.quote: A non-bank PA shall be a company incorporated in India under the Companies Act, 2013.

obligations.text: The Memorandum of Association of the applicant entity should cover the proposed activity of operating as a PA.
obligations.quote: The Memorandum of Association of the applicant entity should cover the proposed activity of operating as a PA.

obligations.text: A PA holding a CoA and already carrying on business as a PA-P, desirous of commencing business in another PA category, shall intimate RBI at least 30 days prior to commencing the new business.
obligations.applies_to: PA holding a Certificate of Authorisation already carrying on PA-P business
obligations.deadline: at least 30 days prior to commencing the new business
obligations.quote: desirous of commencing business in another PA category – shall intimate RBI at least 30 days prior to commencing the new business.

obligations.text: An entity whose application for PA-O or PA-CB CoA is under consideration of RBI shall intimate RBI about its existing PA-P business, if any, through the online portal.
obligations.applies_to: entity whose application for CoA for PA-O or PA-CB is under consideration of RBI
obligations.quote: shall intimate the Reserve Bank about its existing PA-P business, if any, through the online portal, by December 31, 2025.

obligations.text: An entity carrying on only PA-P business shall apply for authorisation as prescribed in 5(b) by December 31, 2025.
obligations.applies_to: entity carrying on only PA-P business
obligations.quote: An entity carrying on only PA-P business shall apply for authorisation as prescribed in 5 (b) above, by December 31, 2025.

obligations.text: An entity carrying on only PA-P business that fails to apply by the due date shall intimate its banker(s) forthwith.
obligations.applies_to: entity carrying on only PA-P business that fails to apply by due date
obligations.deadline: forthwith after failing to apply by December 31, 2025
obligations.quote: An entity which fails to apply by the due date shall intimate its banker(s) forthwith and wind up its business by February 28, 2026.

obligations.text: An entity carrying on only PA-P business that fails to apply by the due date shall wind up its business.
obligations.applies_to: entity carrying on only PA-P business that fails to apply by due date
obligations.quote: An entity which fails to apply by the due date shall intimate its banker(s) forthwith and wind up its business by February 28, 2026.

obligations.text: An entity seeking authorisation to commence or carry on PA business shall have a minimum net-worth of ₹15 crore at the time of tendering application for authorisation.
obligations.applies_to: An entity seeking authorisation to commence or carry on PA business
obligations.deadline: At the time of tendering application for authorisation
obligations.quote: An entity seeking authorisation to commence or carry on PA business shall have a minimum net-worth of ₹15 crore at the time of tendering application for authorisation

obligations.text: An entity seeking authorisation to commence or carry on PA business shall attain a minimum net-worth of ₹25 crore by the end of the third financial year of grant of authorisation.
obligations.applies_to: An entity seeking authorisation to commence or carry on PA business
obligations.deadline: By the end of third financial year of grant of authorisation
obligations.quote: shall attain a minimum net-worth of ₹25 crore by the end of third financial year of grant of authorisation

obligations.text: The minimum net-worth, as applicable, shall be maintained by a PA on an ongoing basis.
obligations.quote: The minimum networth, as applicable, shall be maintained by a PA on an ongoing basis.

obligations.text: Deferred Tax Assets included in any component of net worth shall be deducted while arriving at the net-worth value.
obligations.quote: if Deferred Tax Assets have been included in any of the components, the same shall be deducted while arriving at the net-worth value.

obligations.text: Compulsorily convertible preference shares shall be compulsorily convertible into equity shares and the shareholder agreements shall specifically prohibit any withdrawal of this preference share capital at any time.
obligations.applies_to: Entity whose net worth includes compulsorily convertible preference shares (shareholder agreements)
obligations.quote: they should be compulsorily convertible into equity shares and the shareholder agreements should specifically prohibit any withdrawal of this preference share capital at any time

obligations.text: An entity seeking PA authorisation shall submit a certificate in the enclosed format (Annexure 2.1) from its statutory auditor evidencing compliance with the applicable net-worth requirement while submitting the application for authorisation.
obligations.deadline: While submitting the application for authorisation
obligations.quote: An entity seeking PA authorisation shall submit a certificate in the enclosed format ( Annexure 2.1 ) from their statutory auditor evidencing compliance with the applicable net-worth requirement while submitting the application for authorisation.

obligations.text: A newly incorporated non-bank entity without an audited statement of financial accounts shall submit a certificate from its statutory auditor regarding current networth along with a provisional balance sheet as of recent date.
obligations.applies_to: A newly incorporated non-bank entity which may not have an audited statement of financial accounts
obligations.quote: A newly incorporated non-bank entity which may not have an audited statement of financial accounts shall submit a certificate in the enclosed format from their statutory auditor regarding current networth

obligations.text: A PA shall be professionally managed.
obligations.quote: A PA shall be professionally managed. The promoters and directors of the entity shall satisfy the fit and proper criteria as below:

obligations.text: The promoters and directors of the PA shall satisfy the fit and proper criteria, including having a record of fairness and integrity (financial integrity, good reputation and character, and honesty).
obligations.applies_to: Promoters and directors of the PA
obligations.quote: The promoters and directors of the entity shall satisfy the fit and proper criteria as below: i. The person has a record of fairness and integrity, including but not limited to:

obligations.text: The promoters and directors of the PA must not have incurred any of the listed disqualifications, including conviction for moral turpitude, economic or RBI-law offences, being an undischarged insolvent, being subject to a subsisting financial-system debarment order, being found of unsound mind, or being financially unsound.
obligations.applies_to: Promoters and directors of the PA
obligations.quote: Such person has not incurred any of the following disqualifications: Convicted by a court for any offence involving moral turpitude or any economic offence

obligations.text: Any takeover, acquisition of control, or change in management of a non-bank PA shall adhere to RBI circular CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S-590/02-14-006/2022-23 dated July 4, 2022, as amended from time to time.
obligations.applies_to: Non-bank PA (including entities whose PA authorisation application is pending with RBI)
obligations.quote: Any takeover or acquisition of control or change in the management of a non-bank PA shall adhere to RBI circular CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S-590/02-14-006/2022-23 dated July 4, 2022

obligations.text: A PA shall have a dispute resolution mechanism to handle payment related disputes in transactions facilitated by it.
obligations.quote: A PA shall have a dispute resolution mechanism to handle payment related disputes in transactions facilitated by it.

obligations.text: The PA's dispute management policy shall ensure adherence to RBI instructions, including on Turn Around Time (TAT) for resolution of failed transactions issued vide DPSS.CO.PD No.629/02.01.014/2019-20 dated September 20, 2019 (as amended from time to time).
obligations.quote: The policy shall ensure adherence to the instructions issued by RBI including on Turn Around Time (TAT) for resolution of failed transactions

obligations.text: Agreements between a PA, its merchants, its acquiring banks and all other stakeholders shall clearly delineate the roles and responsibilities of the involved parties, including manner of refunds, treatment of failed transactions, return policy, grievance redressal and reconciliation.
obligations.applies_to: PA; its merchants; its acquiring banks; all other stakeholders
obligations.quote: Agreements between a PA, its merchants, its acquiring banks, and all other stakeholders shall clearly delineate the roles and responsibilities of the involved parties

obligations.text: The PA shall disclose comprehensive information regarding its merchant policies, privacy policy and other terms and conditions on its website and/or its mobile application.
obligations.quote: The PA shall disclose comprehensive information regarding its merchant policies, privacy policy and other terms and conditions on its website and / or its mobile application.

obligations.text: The PA shall appoint an officer responsible for responding to issues raised by its merchants, along with an escalation matrix for grievance redressal.
obligations.quote: The PA shall appoint an officer responsible for responding to issues raised by its merchants along with an escalation matrix for grievance redressal.

obligations.text: Details of the officer and escalation matrix shall be prominently displayed on the PA's website.
obligations.quote: Details of the officer and escalation matrix shall be prominently displayed on its website.

obligations.text: PA must put in place adequate Information and Data Security infrastructure and systems for detection and prevention of frauds.
obligations.quote: PA shall put in place adequate Information and Data Security infrastructure and systems for detection and prevention of frauds.

obligations.text: PA must ensure that the infrastructure of the merchants is compliant with security standards like PCI-DSS and PCI-SSF, as may be applicable.
obligations.quote: PA shall ensure that infrastructure of the merchants is compliant with security standards like PCI-DSS and PCI-SSF, as may be applicable.

obligations.text: PA must put in place a Board approved Information Security Policy for safety and security of the payment systems it operates, and implement security measures in accordance with that policy to mitigate identified as well as emerging risks.
obligations.quote: PA shall put in place a Board approved Information Security Policy for safety and security of the payment systems operated by it and implement security measures in accordance with the said policy

obligations.text: PA must ensure adherence to the baseline technology-related recommendations provided in Annexure 1.
obligations.quote: PA shall ensure adherence to baseline technology-related recommendations as provided in Annexure 1 .

obligations.text: PA must comply with the data storage requirements applicable to Payment System Operators as laid out in RBI circular DPSS.CO.OD No.2785/06.08.005/2017-2018 dated April 6, 2018, as amended from time to time.
obligations.quote: PA shall comply with data storage requirements as applicable to Payment System Operators (PSOs) as laid out in RBI circular DPSS.CO.OD No.2785/06.08.005/2017-2018 dated April 6, 2018

obligations.text: PA must have an annual system audit, including cyber security audit, conducted by CERT-In empanelled auditors, and submit the report to the respective Regional Office of DPSS, RBI.
obligations.deadline: within such timelines as may be prescribed by RBI
obligations.quote: An annual system audit, including cyber security audit, conducted by CERT-In empanelled auditors shall be carried out and report thereof shall be submitted to the respective Regional Office of DPSS, RBI within such timelines as may be prescribed by RBI.

obligations.text: A PA shall aggregate funds only for the merchant with whom it has a contractual relationship.
obligations.quote: A PA shall aggregate funds only for the merchant with whom it has a contractual relationship.

obligations.text: A PA business shall not carry out marketplace business.
obligations.quote: A PA business shall not carry out marketplace business.

obligations.text: A PA shall ensure that the extant instructions with regard to Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) are followed.
obligations.quote: A PA shall ensure that the extant instructions with regard to Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) are followed.

obligations.text: A PA shall ensure that any charges, other than the price of goods / service / investment amount, charged by a merchant, are distinctly displayed to the payer prior to the transaction.
obligations.quote: A PA shall also ensure that any charges, other than the price of goods / service / investment amount, charged by a merchant, are distinctly displayed to the payer prior to the transaction.

obligations.text: A PA shall not place limits on transaction amount for a particular payment mode.
obligations.quote: A PA shall not place limits on transaction amount for a particular payment mode.

obligations.text: A PA shall not give an option for ATM PIN as a factor of authentication for card-not-present transactions.
obligations.quote: A PA shall not give an option for ATM PIN as a factor of authentication for card-not-present transactions.

obligations.text: All refunds shall be made to the original method of payment, unless specifically instructed by the payer to credit the refund to an alternate mode belonging to the same payer.
obligations.quote: All refunds shall be made to the original method of payment, unless specifically instructed by the payer to credit the refund to an alternate mode belonging to the same payer.

obligations.text: A PA-CB shall keep funds related to inward and outward transactions separate, and no co-mingling of funds or netting off between outward and inward transactions is permitted under any circumstance.
obligations.quote: Funds related to inward and outward transactions as carried out by a PA-CB shall be kept separate. No co-mingling of funds or netting off for outward and inward transactions is permitted under any circumstance.

obligations.text: A PA-CB shall not purchase foreign currency from, or sell foreign currency to, any entity other than an Authorised Dealer (AD).
obligations.quote: A PA-CB shall not purchase foreign currency from, or sell it to, any entity other than an Authorised Dealer (AD).

obligations.text: The maximum value per transaction for inward or outward transactions processed by a PA-CB shall be ₹25 lakh.
obligations.quote: In respect of inward or outward transactions processed by a PA - CB, the maximum value per transaction shall be ₹25 lakh.

obligations.text: AD-I banks maintaining InCAs / OCAs shall ensure that all requirements under FEMA are adhered to.
obligations.applies_to: AD-I banks maintaining Inward Collection Accounts (InCAs) / Outward Collection Accounts (OCAs)
obligations.quote: AD-I banks maintaining Inward Collection Accounts (InCAs) / Outward Collection Accounts (OCAs), as defined in paragraph 16a. below of this MD, shall ensure that all requirements under FEMA are adhered to.

obligations.text: AD-I Bank shall have automated processes to fetch the requisite information from a PA-CB.
obligations.quote: AD-I Bank shall have automated processes to fetch the requisite information from a PA – CB.

obligations.text: The payment transaction (outward or inward) shall be identified as a cross-border transaction to establish its bonafides, and the Payment System Provider shall make provisions for this from such timelines as specified by RBI.
obligations.deadline: From such timelines as specified by RBI
obligations.quote: A Payment System Provider shall make provisions for implementation of the same from such timelines as specified by RBI.

obligations.text: A PA-CB shall provide the documents / information required by the exporter / importer to the AD bank of the exporter / importer for closure of their corresponding EDPMS / IDPMS entry, wherever applicable, in compliance with the extant directions.
obligations.quote: PA – CB shall provide the documents / information required by the exporter / importer to the AD bank of the exporter / importer, for closure of their corresponding entry in Export Data Processing

obligations.text: Settlement in non-INR currencies shall be permitted only for Indian exporters directly onboarded by the PA-CB facilitating inward transactions.
obligations.quote: Settlement in non-INR currencies shall be permitted only for those merchants (Indian exporters) which have been directly onboarded by the PA – CB facilitating inward transactions.

obligations.text: An authorised PA shall submit reports as listed in Annexure 2 of the MD.
obligations.quote: An authorised PA shall submit reports as listed in Annexure 2 of this MD.

obligations.text: A PA shall undertake customer due diligence (CDD) of its merchants in accordance with the MD on KYC.
obligations.quote: A PA shall undertake customer due diligence (CDD) of its merchants in accordance with MD on KYC.

obligations.text: While onboarding, the PA shall, with the merchant's consent, retrieve the merchant's KYC record from CKYCR.
obligations.quote: While onboarding, the PA shall, with the merchant’s consent, retrieve the merchant’s KYC record from CKYCR.

obligations.text: Where a merchant's record is not available in CKYCR, or the PA cannot access CKYCR, the PA shall carry out CDD through other mechanisms outlined in the MD on KYC.
obligations.quote: Where a merchant’s record is not available in CKYCR, or a PA cannot access CKYCR as its application for authorisation is pending with the Reserve Bank, CDD of the merchant could be carried out through other mechanisms outlined in MD on KYC.

obligations.text: A PA shall undertake background and antecedent check of the merchant.
obligations.quote: A PA shall undertake background and antecedent check of the merchant.

obligations.text: A PA shall ensure that a marketplace onboarded by it does not accept payments for a seller not onboarded on to the marketplace's platform.
obligations.quote: A PA shall ensure that a marketplace onboarded by it does not accept payments for a seller not onboarded on to the marketplace’s platform.

obligations.text: PA shall facilitate allotment of appropriate Merchant Category Code and Merchant ID / Terminal ID to its merchants, including those onboarded through an overseas PA.
obligations.quote: PA shall facilitate allotment of appropriate Merchant Category Code and Merchant ID / Terminal ID to its merchants including those onboarded through an overseas PA.

obligations.text: PA shall ensure that the name of the merchant is captured appropriately for all transactions processed for it.
obligations.quote: PA shall ensure that name of the merchant is captured appropriately for all transactions processed for it.

obligations.text: A payment aggregator must put in place necessary validation mechanisms to ensure that funds due to a merchant are credited only in the merchant's bank account.
obligations.quote: Necessary validation mechanisms shall be put in place by a PA to ensure that funds due to a merchant are credited in the merchant’s bank account only.

obligations.text: A PA must monitor transactions subsequently undertaken by merchants to ensure they are in line with the merchant's business profile and must ensure adherence to other aspects of the MD on KYC while conducting its operations.
obligations.quote: The PA must also monitor transactions subsequently undertaken by the merchants to ensure that these transactions are in line with latter’s business profile and ensure adherence to other aspects of MD on KYC

obligations.text: A non-bank PA shall register itself with the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) in compliance with the MD on KYC and meet the reporting requirements listed therein.
obligations.quote: Non-bank PA shall register itself with the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) in compliance with MD on KYC and meet the reporting requirements listed therein.

obligations.text: A PA, including an existing PA whose application is pending with RBI for authorisation, shall ensure that merchants onboarded till December 31, 2025 comply with the above due diligence requirements.
obligations.applies_to: PA, including an existing PA whose application is pending with Reserve Bank of India for authorisation
obligations.deadline: Within one year from the date of this MD
obligations.quote: shall ensure that merchants onboarded till December 31, 2025, comply with the above due diligence requirements within one year from the date of this MD.

obligations.text: From January 1, 2026, merchants should be onboarded in accordance with the due diligence requirements prescribed in this MD.
obligations.quote: From January 1, 2026, merchants should be onboarded in accordance with due diligence requirements prescribed in this MD.

obligations.text: Acquiring bank shall have a policy for processing payments for merchants acquired through an authorised non-bank PA.
obligations.quote: Acquiring bank shall have a policy for processing payments for merchants acquired through an authorised non-bank PA.

obligations.text: Acquiring Bank of a non-bank PA shall ensure that merchants onboarded by the PA are in compliance with the acquiring bank's policy for merchant acquiring.
obligations.applies_to: Acquiring Bank of a non-bank PA
obligations.quote: Acquiring Bank of a non-bank PA shall ensure that merchants onboarded by the PA are in compliance with acquiring bank’s policy for merchant acquiring.

obligations.text: Where agents are employed to assist merchants, the PA shall maintain the details of the agent assisting the merchant.
obligations.quote: PA shall maintain the details of the agent assisting the merchant, where services of such agents are employed.

obligations.text: The non-bank PA shall carry out due diligence of the persons appointed as authorised / designated agents.
obligations.quote: The non-bank PA shall carry out due diligence of the persons appointed as authorised / designated agents.

obligations.text: The ultimate responsibility of due diligence shall lie on the PA, and agents can be used only for the limited purposes prescribed.
obligations.quote: The ultimate responsibility of due diligence shall lie on PA and agents can only be used for limited purposes as prescribed above.

obligations.text: A non-bank PA shall maintain the funds collected on behalf of its merchants in a separate escrow account with any Scheduled Commercial Bank (SCB) in India.
obligations.quote: A non-bank PA shall maintain the funds collected on behalf of its merchants in a separate escrow account with any Scheduled Commercial Bank (SCB) in India.

obligations.text: The instructions in Table 1 on operations in escrow accounts must be adhered to.
obligations.quote: Details of operations in escrow accounts are incorporated in Table 1 below and the instructions mentioned therein must be adhered to by December 31, 2025.

obligations.text: Escrow accounts shall only be utilised for authorised PA business and not for any other business.
obligations.quote: Such escrow accounts shall only be utilised for authorised PA business and not for any other business.

obligations.text: Inter-escrow account transfers must be supported by an auditor's certificate.
obligations.quote: Inter-escrow A/c transfer Auditor’s certificate needed for such transactions. Not permitted.

obligations.text: A permitted debit must not be used to transfer funds from an entity acting as a BBPOU, as defined in the Master Direction on BBPS, to its BBPS escrow account, except where the entity acts as a PA to an Agent Institution and on its behalf transfers funds to the BBPS escrow account of the BBPOU.
obligations.applies_to: Payment Aggregator (PA) operating the promotional/incentive/cash-back payment received account
obligations.quote: This permitted debit shall not be used to transfer funds from an entity acting as a BBPOU, as defined in Master Direction on BBPS to its BBPS escrow account

obligations.text: Maintain day-end balance in the escrow account not less than the amount realised in escrow towards funds payable to merchants but not yet settled to them.
obligations.quote: Maintenance of day end balance in escrow account Shall not be less than the amount realised in escrow towards funds payable to the merchants, but not settled to them.

obligations.text: No interest shall be payable on balances maintained in the escrow account, except on the core portion amount of the domestic escrow account, subject to the conditions in paragraph 17.
obligations.quote: No interest shall be payable on the balances maintained in the escrow account(s) except on the core portion amount of the domestic escrow account, subject to the conditions prescribed in paragraph 17 below.

obligations.text: Existing PA must migrate funds to an escrow account within two months from the date of authorisation by the Reserve Bank of India.
obligations.deadline: Within two months from the date of authorisation by the Reserve Bank of India
obligations.quote: Escrow a/c by existing PA Within two months from the date of authorisation by the Reserve Bank of India.

obligations.text: Credit funds to the merchant's account as per the agreement between the PA and the merchant, which must be fair, equitable and transparently mention the settlement timelines.
obligations.deadline: As per the agreement between the PA and the merchant
obligations.quote: Such an agreement should be fair, equitable and must transparently mention the settlement timelines.

obligations.text: An entity authorised to carry out PA-O and PA-P businesses shall use the same escrow account for both business activities.
obligations.applies_to: Entity authorised to carry out PA-O and PA-P businesses
obligations.quote: An entity authorised to carry out PA-O and PA-P businesses shall use the same escrow account for both the business activities.

obligations.text: The core portion of the escrow account shall continue to be maintained within the escrow account maintained for PA activity.
obligations.applies_to: Payment aggregators / banks maintaining escrow accounts for PA activity
obligations.quote: The core portion of escrow account shall continue to be maintained within the escrow account maintained for PA activity.

obligations.text: Banks shall not issue any receipt for core portion deposits which may entitle the PA to the funds available in the core portion, and shall not mark any lien on the amount held in such deposits.
obligations.quote: Banks shall not issue any receipt for such deposits which may entitle PA to the funds available in the core portion or mark any lien on the amount held in such form of deposits.

obligations.text: The core portion shall be calculated separately for each escrow account.
obligations.applies_to: Payment aggregators / banks maintaining escrow accounts
obligations.quote: The core portion shall be calculated separately for each escrow account.

obligations.text: The escrow balance maintained shall be clearly disclosed in the auditor's certificates to be submitted to RBI on quarterly and annual basis.
obligations.applies_to: Auditors / payment aggregators submitting auditor's certificates
obligations.quote: The escrow balance maintained shall be clearly disclosed in the auditor’s certificates to be submitted to RBI on quarterly and annual basis.

obligations.text: PA shall submit the list of merchants onboarded by it to the bank where it maintains the escrow account, and update the list prior to initiating settlement to these merchants.
obligations.deadline: Prior to initiating settlement to merchants (list to be updated before each settlement)
obligations.quote: PA shall submit the list of merchants onboarded by it to the bank where it is maintaining the escrow account and update the list prior to initiating settlement to these merchants.

obligations.text: The bank shall ensure that payments are made only to eligible merchants and for permissible debits or credits as defined under this MD.
obligations.quote: The bank shall ensure that payments are made only to eligible merchants and for permissible debits or credits as defined under this MD.

obligations.text: There shall be an exclusive clause in the agreement between the PA and the bank maintaining the escrow account restricting usage of escrow balance only to permissible debits or credits in Table 1.
obligations.applies_to: PA and bank maintaining escrow account
obligations.quote: There shall be an exclusive clause in the agreement signed between the PA and the bank maintaining escrow account towards usage of balance in escrow account only as per the permissible debits or credits as mentioned in Table 1 above.

obligations.text: The escrow account shall not be operated for 'Cash-on-Delivery' transactions.
obligations.quote: The escrow account shall not be operated for ‘Cash-on-Delivery’ transactions.

obligations.text: Onward transfer of outward transaction funds to foreign merchants shall be carried out only by debit to the OCA.
obligations.quote: Onward transfer to the foreign merchants shall be carried out only by debit to the OCA.

obligations.text: For a PA-CB also engaged in domestic PA activity, InCA and OCA shall be kept separate from the escrow account(s) opened for domestic PA activity.
obligations.applies_to: PA-CB engaged in domestic PA activity
obligations.quote: In case a PA-CB also engages in domestic PA activity, InCA and OCA shall be kept separate from the escrow account(s) opened for such domestic PA activity.

obligations.text: Authorised entities shall submit a certificate, signed by the statutory auditor(s), to the respective Regional Office of DPSS, RBI where the registered office of PA is situated, certifying compliance with escrow account balance maintenance instructions, at the periodicity prescribed in Annexure 2.
obligations.deadline: As per periodicity prescribed in Annexure 2
obligations.quote: A certificate, signed by the statutory auditor(s), shall be submitted by the authorised entities to the respective Regional Office of DPSS, RBI, where registered office of PA is situated

obligations.text: Where an additional escrow account is maintained, balances in both accounts shall be considered for the certification and separately mentioned in the certificate.
obligations.applies_to: authorised entities (PA) maintaining an additional escrow account
obligations.quote: In case an additional escrow account is being maintained, it shall be ensured that balances in both accounts are considered for the above certification and that these are separately mentioned in the certificate.

obligations.text: Certificates shall be submitted separately for domestic activity (PA-O/P) and cross border activity (PA-CB).
obligations.quote: The certificates shall be submitted separately for domestic activity, i.e. PA – O / P and cross border activity, i.e. PA – CB.

obligations.text: When there is a need to shift the escrow account from one bank to another, the shift shall be effected in a time-bound manner without impacting the payment cycle to merchants, under advice to RBI.
obligations.quote: In case there is a need to shift the escrow account from one bank to another, the same shall be effected in a time-bound manner without impacting the payment cycle to merchants, under advice to RBI.

obligations.text: For maintenance of reserve requirements, the outstanding balance in the escrow account shall be part of net demand and time liabilities (NDTL), computed on the basis of balances appearing in the books of the bank as on the date of reporting.
obligations.applies_to: Banks maintaining escrow accounts for payment aggregators
obligations.quote: For banks, the outstanding balance in the escrow account shall be part of the ‘net demand and time liabilities’ (NDTL) for the purposes of maintenance of reserve requirements.

obligations.text: Credits towards reversed transactions and refund transactions shall be routed back through the escrow account, unless the refund is directly managed by the merchant and the payer has been made aware of the same as per the PA-merchant contract.
obligations.quote: Credits towards reversed transactions (where funds are received by PA) and refund transactions shall be routed back through the escrow account unless the refund is directly managed by the merchant

obligations.text: The chargeback rights of customers, as applicable, shall remain unaffected.
obligations.quote: The chargeback rights of customers, as applicable, shall remain unaffected.

obligations.text: The entities shall at a minimum carry out a comprehensive security risk assessment of their people, IT, business process environment, etc., to identify risk exposures with remedial measures and residual risks.
obligations.quote: The entities at a minimum shall carry out comprehensive security risk assessment of their people, IT, business process environment, etc., to identify risk exposures with remedial measures and residual risks.

obligations.text: Reports on risk assessment, security compliance posture, security audit reports and security incidents shall be presented to the Board.
obligations.quote: Reports on risk assessment, security compliance posture, security audit reports and security incidents shall be presented to the Board.

obligations.text: Data security standards and best practices like PCI-DSS, PCI-SSF, latest encryption standards, transport channel security, etc., shall be implemented.

ratings.finding: FlexiPay is authorised as an online Payment Aggregator (PA-O) and FlexiCredit is an NBFC-ICC, and neither is described as an AD Category-II authorised entity facilitating current account transactions, so the restriction on PA-CB business does not apply to them.

ratings.policy_quote: FlexiPay is authorised by the RBI under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 as an online Payment Aggregator (PA-O).
ratings.finding: The policy records that FlexiPay, a non-bank, holds RBI authorisation as a PA-O, granted March 2023, so the authorisation step is covered, though the portal submission process itself is not described.

No profile material shows FlexiPay or FlexiCredit being regulated by another financial sector regulator, and FlexiPay's PA authorisation has already been granted, so the NOC-based application timeline does not apply.

ratings.policy_quote: FlexiPay India Private Limited ("FlexiPay") is a payments company incorporated in 2019 and headquartered in Bengaluru.
ratings.finding: FlexiPay is a Private Limited company incorporated in 2019, which is consistent with a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, although the policy does not name the Act.
No policy paragraph addresses whether FlexiPay's Memorandum of Association covers the operation of a payment aggregator.
FlexiPay holds PA-O authorisation, not a PA-P Certificate of Authorisation, so the 30-day intimation rule does not apply.
FlexiPay's PA-O authorisation was granted in March 2023 and no pending PA-O or PA-CB application is shown, so this intimation rule does not apply.
FlexiPay is not an entity carrying on only PA-P business, since it is an authorised PA-O, so this rule does not apply.
FlexiPay is not an entity carrying on only PA-P business, so the banker-intimation rule for failure to apply does not apply.
FlexiPay is not an entity carrying on only PA-P business, so the wind-up requirement for failure to apply does not apply.
The rule covers entities seeking PA authorisation at application, but FlexiPay was already authorised in March 2023, so it does not apply.

ratings.policy_quote: FlexiPay's net worth was ₹16 crore on 31 March 2026, the end of the third full financial year since it was authorised as a PA.
ratings.finding: The policy records net worth of ₹16 crore at the end of the third financial year after authorisation, which is below the required ₹25 crore, and no policy paragraph sets or tracks the ₹25 crore target.
ratings.action: Raise FlexiPay's net worth to at least ₹25 crore immediately, and add a policy paragraph stating the ₹25 crore requirement and the steps taken to meet it.

ratings.policy_quote: Finance tracks FlexiPay's net worth every quarter and reports it to the Board.
ratings.finding: The policy only requires quarterly tracking and Board reporting, with no obligation to maintain the minimum, and net worth of ₹16 crore is below the applicable ₹25 crore minimum.
ratings.action: Add a requirement to maintain the applicable minimum net worth on an ongoing basis, with escalation to the Board and a remediation plan whenever net worth falls below it.

ratings.finding: No policy paragraph deals with deducting deferred tax assets from net worth.
The company profile does not show that FlexiPay's net worth includes compulsorily convertible preference shares, so the rule does not apply.
The auditor certificate is required when applying for authorisation, and FlexiPay was already authorised in March 2023, so the rule does not apply.
FlexiPay was incorporated in 2019 and has audited financial statements, so the rule for newly incorporated entities without audited accounts does not apply.
No paragraph shown addresses professional management of the PA; the governance paragraphs cover fraud oversight and compliance review only.
No paragraph shown sets fit and proper criteria for promoters and directors, including fairness and integrity.
No paragraph shown screens promoters and directors for the listed disqualifications.
No paragraph shown addresses takeover, acquisition of control, or change in management of FlexiPay, which is a non-bank PA, or adherence to the July 2022 RBI circular.

ratings.policy_quote: If a complaint is rejected in full or in part, or not resolved within 30 days, the reply tells the customer they may complain to the RBI

ratings.action: Extend the grievance policy or add a dispute procedure that covers merchant and payment disputes on PA transactions, with steps and timelines.

ratings.policy_quote: A failed FlexiPay Checkout payment where the customer was debited is refunded to the source within T+5 days.
ratings.finding: FP-09 sets refunds for failed Checkout payments within T+5 days and reversal of failed UPI or wallet debits by T+1 day, which meets the RBI failed-transaction TAT.

ratings.policy_quote: Permitted credits: payments from customers, refunds and reversals from merchants, and pre-funding by FlexiPay.

ratings.action: Write the roles for refunds, failed transactions, return policy, grievance redressal and reconciliation into the merchant and acquiring bank agreements.

ratings.finding: No policy paragraph shows disclosure of merchant policies, privacy policy or terms and conditions on the website or mobile app.

No policy paragraph appoints an officer for merchant issues or sets an escrow-style escalation matrix for merchant grievances; the Principal Nodal Officer named in the profile is for grievances without a merchant scope.
No policy paragraph requires the officer and escalation matrix to be displayed prominently on the PA website.

No policy paragraph shown requires merchant infrastructure to comply with PCI-DSS or PCI-SSF.

ratings.policy_quote: The Board approves this policy.

The rule applies only to PA-CB (cross-border payment aggregators); FlexiPay is authorised as an online PA-O, so it does not carry on cross-border PA-CB activity under this rule.
The rule applies only to PA-CB entities buying or selling foreign currency; FlexiPay is a PA-O and does not deal in foreign currency under this authorisation.
The ₹25 lakh per-transaction cap applies to PA-CB inward and outward transactions; FlexiPay is a PA-O and no cross-border cap is set in its policies, which is outside this rule's scope.
The rule applies to AD-I banks maintaining InCAs or OCAs; FlexiPay is a payments company, not an AD-I bank.
The rule applies to AD-I banks fetching information from a PA-CB; FlexiPay is neither an AD-I bank nor a PA-CB.

ratings.action: Add a step to FP-20 §4.1 that flags every cross-border transaction at FlexiPay Checkout so it can be identified, and set the implementation date to the timeline RBI specifies.

ratings.finding: The rule applies to PA-CB entities providing exporter or importer documents for EDPMS or IDPMS closure; FlexiPay is a PA-O and does not facilitate such cross-border trade transactions under this authorisation.
The rule on non-INR settlement applies only to PA-CB entities facilitating inward transactions; FlexiPay is a PA-O and this restriction does not apply to it.
The policies reviewed contain no paragraph on submitting the Annexure 2 reports required of an authorised PA.

ratings.policy_quote: Every merchant completes KYC as a legal entity (PAN, certificate of incorporation or registration, GST certificate where applicable, and KYC of the beneficial owners and authorised signatories).
ratings.finding: FP-03 §2.1 sets out legal-entity KYC documents and beneficial owner checks, but it does not tie merchant CDD to the MD on KYC.
ratings.action: Amend FP-03 §2.1 to state that merchant CDD is carried out in accordance with the RBI Master Direction on KYC.

ratings.finding: No paragraph requires retrieving merchant KYC records from CKYCR with the merchant's consent during onboarding.
No paragraph provides for alternative merchant CDD where a CKYCR record is unavailable or CKYCR cannot be accessed.
No paragraph requires a background and antecedent check of merchants; FP-03 covers only KYC documents and website review.
The company profile describes no marketplace onboarding activity, so the marketplace seller rule does not apply.
No paragraph covers allotting Merchant Category Codes or Merchant ID / Terminal IDs to merchants.
No paragraph requires the merchant name to be captured for transactions processed for merchants.

ratings.policy_quote: All amounts collected from customers for merchants are credited to FlexiPay's escrow account with Coastal Commercial Bank.
ratings.finding: The policy routes merchant funds through an escrow account and permits debits to merchants, but it does not describe any validation mechanism that ensures funds due to a merchant are credited only to the merchant's own bank account.
ratings.action: Add a documented validation step in FP-12 that checks each merchant payout against the merchant's registered bank account before crediting.

ratings.policy_quote: Transaction monitoring flags spikes in volume, refunds above 10% and chargebacks above 1% of transactions for review within 2 working days.
ratings.finding: Merchant transactions are monitored for volume, refunds and chargebacks and against CCO-approved scenarios, but no paragraph requires checking that transactions match the merchant's business profile or aligns monitoring with the KYC MD.
ratings.action: Add a monitoring check in FP-03 that compares each merchant's transactions against its declared business profile and records adherence to the KYC MD.

ratings.action: Add to FP-02 a requirement that FlexiPay registers with FIU-IND as a non-bank PA and meets the reporting requirements of the KYC MD.

ratings.finding: No policy paragraph requires FlexiPay to bring merchants onboarded before 31 December 2025 into compliance with the due diligence requirements.
FP-01 says merchants are onboarded under FP-03, but no shown paragraph sets out the due diligence requirements that merchants onboarded from 1 January 2026 must meet.
This obligation applies to acquiring banks, and FlexiPay is a non-bank PA, not a bank.
This obligation applies to the acquiring bank of a non-bank PA, and FlexiPay is the PA rather than a bank.

No policy paragraph shown places ultimate due diligence responsibility on FlexiPay for agents or limits agent use to prescribed purposes.

ratings.policy_quote: All amounts collected from customers for merchants are credited to FlexiPay's escrow account with Coastal Commercial Bank.

ratings.policy_quote: Permitted credits: payments from customers, refunds and reversals from merchants, and pre-funding by FlexiPay.

ratings.action: Remove the crediting of escrow interest to FlexiPay's own account in FP-12 §4.1 and align all escrow credits and debits with the Table 1 instructions.

ratings.action: Hold FlexiWallet balances in a separate account and keep the PA escrow account limited to merchant collections and settlements.

ratings.policy_quote: A chartered accountant certifies every quarter that the escrow account was operated as these rules require

ratings.action: Add a requirement in FP-12 §5.1 that every inter-escrow account transfer is supported by an auditor's certificate.

ratings.finding: The obligation concerns a BBPOU's BBPS escrow account and a PA operating a promotional, incentive or cash-back payment received account, but the company profile shows FlexiPay as a PA-O, UPI TPAP and PPI issuer with no BBPOU role or promotional/cash-back account, so no policy paragraph is needed.

ratings.policy_quote: The escrow balance is reconciled with merchant payables every day by 10 am the next working day.

ratings.action: Require that the day-end escrow balance is never less than the realised amount payable to merchants, and remove the ₹10,000 tolerance for shortfalls.

ratings.policy_quote: FlexiPay receives interest on 15% of the average escrow balance each month, credited to FlexiPay's own account.

ratings.action: Stop receiving interest on escrow balances outside the permitted core portion of the domestic escrow account and amend the Coastal Commercial Bank arrangement accordingly.

ratings.finding: No paragraph in the policy set deals with migrating existing merchant funds to an escrow account within two months of RBI authorisation.

No policy paragraph describes how the escrow account is shifted from one bank to another, or the time-bound process and advice to RBI that the rule requires.
This reserve requirement applies to banks maintaining escrow accounts for payment aggregators, and FlexiPay is a payment aggregator, not a bank.

ratings.policy_quote: Permitted credits: payments from customers, refunds and reversals from merchants, and pre-funding by FlexiPay.
ratings.finding: FP-12 routes customer payments, merchant refunds and reversals, and customer refunds through the escrow account, which meets the requirement to route reversal and refund credits back through escrow.
No policy paragraph states that customers' chargeback rights remain unaffected; FP-03 §5.1 only lists chargebacks as a merchant agreement term.
No paragraph shown requires a comprehensive security risk assessment covering people, IT, and business processes with remedial measures and residual risks.

ratings.policy_quote: The CISO reports to the CEO and presents the information security posture to the IT Strategy Committee.
ratings.finding: The policy sends the security posture to the IT Strategy Committee, but it does not require risk assessments, compliance posture, audit reports and security incidents to be presented to the Board.
ratings.action: Require the CISO to present risk assessments, security compliance posture, security audit reports and security incidents to the Board, not only to the IT Strategy Committee.

ratings.policy_quote: AES-256 encryption at rest; TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
ratings.finding: The policy covers encryption at rest and transport channel security but does not mention PCI-DSS or PCI-SSF data security standards.
ratings.action: Add a requirement to implement PCI-DSS and PCI-SSF data security standards alongside the existing encryption and transport controls.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown requires reporting security incidents and card holder data breaches to RBI within the stipulated timeframe.
No paragraph shown requires monthly cyber security incident reports with root cause analysis and preventive actions to be submitted to RBI.
No paragraph shown requires a security assessment of merchants during onboarding to check minimum baseline security controls.

ratings.policy_quote: Internal audit is outsourced to a chartered accountant firm and reports to the Audit Committee.
ratings.finding: The policy outsources internal audit to a CA firm reporting to the Audit Committee, but it sets no quarterly internal or annual external audit reports and no submission to the IT Committee.
ratings.action: Require quarterly internal and annual external audit reports covering IT, submitted to the IT Committee.

ratings.policy_quote: An external firm performs a penetration test of the FlexiPay app and Checkout once a year.
ratings.finding: The policy requires an external penetration test once a year, while the rule requires bi-annual VAPT reports submitted to the IT Committee.
ratings.action: Increase external VAPT to twice a year and submit the reports to the IT Committee.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown covers PCI-DSS AOC and ROC reports, observations, or corrective action closure dates submitted to the IT Committee.

ratings.policy_quote: Every information asset has a named owner and a classification (public, internal, confidential, restricted).
ratings.finding: The policy requires an asset owner and classification for information assets but does not require an inventory of applications storing customer sensitive data or its submission to the IT Committee.
ratings.action: Maintain an inventory of applications that store, process or transmit customer sensitive data and submit it to the IT Committee.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown covers PCI-SSF compliance status for payment applications that store or process cardholder data.

ratings.policy_quote: A policy is reviewed at least once a year, and earlier when a regulation it implements changes.
ratings.finding: The policy requires every policy, including information security, to be reviewed at least annually, though Board approval is not stated.

ratings.policy_quote: Every information asset has a named owner and a classification (public, internal, confidential, restricted).
ratings.finding: The information security policy covers asset ownership and data classification but does not address business alignment, roles and responsibilities, training, or penal measures for non-compliance.
ratings.action: Add business alignment, roles and responsibilities, training and penal measures for non-compliance to the information security policy.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown requires a framed IT policy with documented and implemented procedures for regular IT function management.

ratings.policy_quote: A policy is reviewed at least once a year, and earlier when a regulation it implements changes.
ratings.finding: The policy requires annual review of every policy, but it does not name the strategic plan, and the IT policy is only covered by the general rule.
ratings.action: State explicitly that the strategic plan and IT policy are reviewed annually.

ratings.policy_quote: The Board approves this policy. The CISO reports to the CEO and presents the information security posture to the IT Strategy Committee.
ratings.finding: The policy shows the Board approving the information security policy, but nothing shows the Board establishing the necessary organisational processes and functions for information security or providing the necessary resources.
ratings.action: Add a provision in FP-05 or FP-18 stating that the Board establishes the information security processes and functions and provides the resources needed for them.

ratings.policy_quote: The IT Strategy Committee meets once a year.
ratings.finding: The policy has an IT Strategy Committee that meets only once a year, with no business-function representation and no role in assisting Executive Management to implement IT strategy, so it falls short of an IT Steering Committee with well-defined objectives and actions.
ratings.action: Establish an IT Steering Committee with representatives from business functions that meets regularly and has defined objectives and actions to assist Executive Management in implementing the IT strategy.

ratings.finding: No policy paragraph shown deals with an enterprise information model.

ratings.policy_quote: Contain, preserve evidence, eradicate, recover, then review.
ratings.finding: The incident response procedure covers containment, eradication and recovery but has no detection component and does not say the crisis management plan is approved by the IT strategic committee.
ratings.action: Add a Cyber Crisis Management Plan to FP-06 with Detection, Containment, Response and Recovery components, approved by the IT Strategy Committee.

ratings.finding: No policy paragraph shown deals with an enterprise data dictionary or data syntax rules.

ratings.policy_quote: Every information asset has a named owner and a classification (public, internal, confidential, restricted).
ratings.finding: The policy assigns owners and classifications to information assets but does not require identifying threat/vulnerability combinations or assessing the likelihood of impact on confidentiality, availability or integrity.
ratings.action: Add a risk assessment step to FP-05 that, for each in-scope asset, records threat/vulnerability combinations and likelihood of impact on confidentiality, availability and integrity from business, compliance and contractual perspectives.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown sets documented standards or procedures for administering application systems that are approved by the application owner and kept up to date.

ratings.policy_quote: Production systems are reached only through a bastion host with multi-factor authentication. Privileged access is granted for a fixed time and every session is logged.
ratings.finding: The policy controls production access through a bastion host, time-limited privileged access and six-monthly reviews, but never states the least-privilege and need-to-know principle tied to job responsibilities.
ratings.action: Amend FP-05 access control to state that access is granted on least privilege and need to know commensurate with each job role.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown requires assessing skill-set requirements for IT staff or periodically reviewing their training needs.
No paragraph shown requires technology support SLAs covering BCP-DR and data management to include clauses permitting regulatory access; the vendor review in FP-07 covers monitoring only.
No paragraph shown considers assessing IT maturity against international standards or maintaining an action plan to reach a target maturity level.

ratings.policy_quote: AES-256 encryption at rest; TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
ratings.finding: The policy specifies AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, which are well-established international standards.

ratings.policy_quote: Logs from production systems go to a SIEM watched by an outsourced Security Operations Centre, 24 hours a day.
ratings.finding: The policy sends logs from production systems to a 24x7 SIEM, but does not cover security events from endpoint, network, middleware, database, web services, cryptographic events or other infrastructure sources, nor state that they are investigated and analysed.
ratings.action: Extend the SIEM collection scope in FP-05 to all listed event sources (application, endpoint, network, middleware, database, web services, cryptographic events) and require investigation and analysis of them.

ratings.finding: No paragraph shown requires data to be stored in infrastructure outside external jurisdictions.

ratings.policy_quote: Production systems are reached only through a bastion host with multi-factor authentication.
ratings.finding: The policy restricts production access through an MFA-protected bastion host with time-limited, logged privileged access, which controls unauthorised access to data.
No paragraph shown sets outsourcing agreement right-to-audit clauses or annual independent security audit reports from third parties; FP-07 is indexed but its text is not provided.
No paragraph shown requires payment applications to be developed per PCI-SSF guidelines.

ratings.policy_quote: Merchants are contractually barred from storing card data.
ratings.finding: The policy bars merchants from storing card data, but does not require reviewing merchants' PCI-DSS compliance status during onboarding.
ratings.action: Add a PCI-DSS compliance status review step to the merchant onboarding procedure in FP-03.

ratings.policy_quote: FlexiPay Checkout does not store card numbers.
ratings.finding: The policy states that Checkout does not store card numbers and that merchants are contractually barred from storing card data, which matches the rule against storing card credentials in merchant-accessed databases or servers.

No paragraph states whether an ATM PIN is accepted as a factor for card-not-present transactions; the cited authentication paragraphs list only the card issuer's SMS OTP and the card network's additional factor.

ratings.policy_quote: All payment system data (customer details, payment credentials and transaction records) is stored only on servers in India
ratings.finding: The policy requires all payment system data to be stored only on servers in India, with disaster-recovery copies also in India, which satisfies the storage instruction.

ratings.policy_quote: is refunded to the source within T+5 days.
ratings.finding: The policy refunds failed Checkout payments to the source, which is the original payment method, but it does not cover refunds generally or state that any alternate mode requires the customer's specific agreement.
ratings.action: Extend the refund paragraph to all refunds, stating that they go to the original payment method unless the customer specifically agrees to an alternate mode.

ratings.policy_quote: Finance tracks FlexiPay's net worth every quarter and reports it to the Board.
ratings.finding: The policy has quarterly net-worth tracking reported to the Board, but it does not provide for an annual audited report with a statutory auditor certificate on net-worth submitted to RBI by September 30.
ratings.action: Add an annual step to submit the audited report with statutory auditor certificate on net-worth to RBI by September 30.

ratings.policy_quote: Vulnerability scans run monthly on internet-facing systems. An external firm performs a penetration test of the FlexiPay app and Checkout once a year.
ratings.finding: The policy has an annual external penetration test and internal audit by a chartered accountant firm, but it has no externally audited IS Audit Report or Cyber Security Audit Report, no recorded observations with corrective action and closure dates, and no scope covering all information system areas.
ratings.action: Require an externally audited IS Audit and Cyber Security Audit covering all information system processes and applications, with observations, corrective actions and closure dates, and its submission to RBI as prescribed.

ratings.policy_quote: A chartered accountant certifies every quarter that the escrow account was operated as these rules require, and the certificate is sent to the bank.
ratings.finding: The policy requires a quarterly chartered accountant certificate on escrow operation, but it is sent to the bank and sets no deadline of the 15th of the month following quarter end, and it does not specify a certificate on maintenance of balance in escrow account for RBI.
ratings.action: Specify that the auditor's certificate on maintenance of balance in the escrow account is submitted to RBI by the 15th of the month following each quarter end.

ratings.policy_quote: A chartered accountant certifies every quarter that the escrow account was operated as these rules require, and the certificate is sent to the bank.
ratings.finding: The policy has a quarterly chartered accountant certificate on escrow operation, but it is not an internally audited Bankers' Certificate on escrow debits and credits and sets no 15th-of-month submission deadline.
ratings.action: Add an internally audited Bankers' Certificate on escrow account debits and credits, submitted to RBI by the 15th of the month following each quarter end.

No policy paragraph deals with the monthly Statistics of Transactions Handled submission due by the 7th of the next month.
No policy paragraph deals with a Director's declaration and undertaking on changes in the Board of Directors when they happen.
